articles.title: Raffy Tulfo wants impeachment court spox sanctioned
articles.summary: Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo on Monday asked the Senate impeachment court to admonish its spokesperson, lawyer Reginald Tongol, for telling the media that the verdict in the impeachment trial of Vice…

blocks.text: Published October 5, 2026 10:59am

Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo on Monday asked the Senate impeachment court to admonish its spokesperson, lawyer Reginald Tongol, for telling the media that the verdict in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte would be out by December 16.
Tulfo made the call amid an earlier stern warning from the court to the prosecution and defense panel spokespersons against making pronouncements to the media.

“Maybe we should give a warning to our spokesperson. People were calling me over the weekend, saying we have prejudged the outcome since Atty. Tongol told the media that we will have a final verdict by December 16,” Tulfo said during Day 33 of the impeachment trial.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said Tongol's announcement was based on the pre-trial order, which set the schedule for the proceedings.
Escudero said the December 16 date was arrived at through a mathematical computation, based on the 61 days requested by the prosecution to present its evidence and the 30 days sought by the defense.
“That is based on the calendar in the pre-trial order. It is based on math. It is not based on the realities on the ground,” Escudero said.
“It (Tongol's statement) is not the point of view of the court,” he added.
Tulfo, however, stood by his call.
“It is about time we admonish him. This is not the first time. Maraming beses na syang sumablay, pumalpak," he said.
(He has made mistakes and failed many times. Good for him, he seems to know a lot, but we, the senator-judges, my colleagues, there are things we don't know.)

"Buti pa sya marami siyang alam, eh itong mga senator-judges mga kasamahan ko there are things na hindi namin alam, nabubulaga na lamang kami kapag nagdakdak sya sa media, kumbaga inuunahan nya tayo, pine-preempt nya tayo,” Tulfo said.
(We are simply caught off guard when he speaks to the media. In other words, he gets ahead of us and preempts us.)
Escudero responded that he would take the matter "in advisement."— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Who is AMLC Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura?
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court on Monday resumed hearings on Vice President Sara Duterte's alleged unexplained wealth, after a "strategic procedural pause" so both the defense and prosecution panels…

blocks.text: Published October 5, 2026 10:30am

The Senate impeachment court on Monday resumed hearings on Vice President Sara Duterte's alleged unexplained wealth, after a "strategic procedural pause" so both the defense and prosecution panels could prepare for a series of whole-day sessions.
The prosecution team presented Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura to the impeachment tribunal.
Buenaventura assumed the AMLC executive director position on April 14, 2026, after his predecessor, Matthew David, requested a transfer to another post within the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP).

Before his appointment, Buenaventura served as acting deputy director of the Commitments and Policy Group of the AMLC Secretariat, where he played a role in facilitating the Philippines' exit from the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) "grey list."
He also worked as acting legal officer IV at the Office of the General Counsel and Legal Services of the BSP.

Prior to joining AMLC, Buenaventura was the vice president of a financial technology company, where he handled anti-money laundering compliance and regulatory and policy analysis of global financial trends.
He obtained his Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from the University of the Philippines and later graduated magna cum laude from the Bulacan State University College of Law.
Buenaventura later became an associate solicitor at the Office of the Solicitor General and placed 10th in the 2015 Bar Examinations.
He also holds a Master of Corporate Law degree from the University of Cambridge and a Master of Arts in Philosophy from the University of the Philippines.

In April, Buenaventura disclosed that bank transactions totaling P6.7 billion—classified as covered and suspicious—were recorded under the names of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio.
Of the total amount, P3.7 billion was attributed to the Vice President, while P2.998 billion was linked to Carpio.
The AMLC report submitted to the House committee on justice also identified P791 million in transactions as having undetermined inflows and outflows. — VDV/AOL, GMA News

items: The prosecution is presenting Vice President Sara Duterte's financial records to the Senate impeachment court, with key evidence coming from the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) regarding transactions linked to her and her husband.
AMLC reports include covered transactions, which are automatically reported due to their size, and suspicious transactions, which are reported based on specific circumstances that raise concerns.

The interpretation of AMLC reports requires careful analysis, as not all transactions flagged indicate illicit activity; context and the nature of the transactions are crucial for determining legality.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – As the Senate impeachment court conducts hearings on the presentation of Vice President Sara Duterte’s financial records in relation to her alleged unexplained wealth, some of the key pieces of evidence will come from reports submitted to the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) covering potentially billions of pesos in transactions linked to Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio.

The records, along with testimonies and records from the associated banks, could make or break the prosecution’s case on the allegations of unexplained wealth and inaccurate asset declarations against the Vice President. But the evidence presented by AMLC needs to be read carefully.
A transaction appearing in an AMLC report does not, by itself, mean that the money was illicit or that a crime was committed.

There are generally two types of transactions that the AMLC would look into. These are covered transactions, which automatically trigger reporting because of their size, and suspicious transactions, which are reported because of the circumstances surrounding them.

For banks and most financial institutions, a covered transaction report (CTR) is automatically triggered when a cash transaction or its equivalent above P500,000 is made within one banking day. The threshold serves as a reporting trigger, not a judgment that the money is illicit.

A suspicious transaction report is different. There is no automatic threshold. Instead, banks and other covered institutions check transactions based on circumstances defined under the Anti-Money Laundering Act. If the institution determines that a transaction meets any of these, it is required to file an STR with the AMLC.

The law identifies several criteria that can raise suspicion, including when there is no apparent legal, business, or economic purpose; the customer cannot be properly identified; the amount is inconsistent with the person’s known business or financial capacity; transactions appear structured to avoid reporting requirements; or the transaction appears connected to an unlawful activity, among others. (READ: Why didn’t banks flag large check encashments by Sara Duterte staff?)
A more comprehensive list of reasons for STR filings is shown in the graphic below:

In practice, this means banks look beyond the size of a transfer. AMLC guidance says a transaction may be considered unusual when its amount, origin, destination or type is inconsistent with the customer’s known legitimate activities.

A large payment can have a perfectly ordinary explanation, such as the sale of property or an investment redemption. Conversely, a much smaller payment can prompt an STR if its source, recipient, or purpose raises concerns.

The questions investigators would typically want answered include who sent and received the money, where it came from, where it ultimately went, what the transaction was for, whether there are documents supporting that explanation, and whether the amount fits the customer’s known income, assets and usual financial activity.

AMLC records have figured in several high-profile cases. During the 2012 impeachment trial of then-chief justice Renato Corona, Ombudsman Conchita Carpio-Morales testified on an AMLC report detailing hundreds of transactions in accounts attributed to Corona.
In the pork barrel cases, AMLC testimony and bank records helped trace the movement of government funds through NGO accounts linked to Janet Lim Napoles. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Jane Doe at centre of Cornell rape case targeted with threats, her lawyer says
articles.summary: The woman who has alleged she was drugged and raped by ‌Cornell University students has been the target of threats, her lawyer said on Sunday.

image.caption: Students walk past the entrance of Cornell University in Ithaca, N.Y., on Thursday. (Lauren Petracca/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
The woman who has alleged she was drugged and raped by ‌Cornell University students has been the target of threats, her lawyer said on Sunday.
Cornell under scrutiny following outcry over university's handling of allegations

Thomas Giuffra, who represents the woman identified as Jane Doe, told CNN that people have threatened to silence or harm her if she does not withdraw her civil lawsuit alleging that several members of a Cornell fraternity drugged and ​raped her in 2024.
"She's received multiple threats," Giuffra said on CNN's State ​of the Union, adding that he had also been threatened.

"I'm not afraid of these people," he said. "But the threats, the abuse to protect what's going on, the status quo — these guys are ​disgusting. They should stay in their mother's basement and stay out of the world."

The identity of ⁠Jane Doe has become ⁠part of the fevered online conversation surrounding the case. Women ‌on social media have been posting #IamJaneDoe in solidarity with the accuser and to counter some who have sought to publicly name her.
Advocate calls for 'overhaul' of student groups to address harms on campuses like Cornell

Michael Tracey, an independent journalist and commentator, posted on Friday what he said was the accuser's name, which Reuters was unable to verify, before quickly deleting it, saying his point had been ⁠made.

He has expressed sympathy for the accused men over what he says is the harassment they have faced and described his effort to name the Cornell accuser as journalistic diligence protected under the U.S. Constitution as free speech.

items: What to know about Cornell's alleged frat house gang-rape case and the 'Cornell 7'
'I am Jane Doe': Online rally to protect Cornell rape accuser's identity becomes a reckoning

blocks.text: He told Reuters on Sunday ‌that he did not wish to encourage threats or harassment against the woman.

"The point, from my perspective, was more about the public-policy implications of this increasingly commonly used tactic in civil litigation, for plaintiffs' attorneys to introduce sensational, reputation-harming allegations using the cloak of anonymity for their clients," Tracey said in an interview.
N.Y. governor appoints special prosecutor to Cornell sexual assault case

Cornell University president ​Michael Kotlikoff said in a video message on Saturday that the university will examine the role of fraternities and sororities on campus following the outcry over the ⁠school's handling of the rape allegations.

"At their best, these organizations can provide students with friendship, belonging, mentorship and a ⁠powerful sense of community," he said. "But being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility."
Since the lawsuit was ⁠filed last ⁠month, prosecutors in New York's Tompkins County have ​been criticized for their initial handling of the allegations in 2024.

items: Cornell president calls alleged gang rape 'deeply disturbing,' pledges greater transparency

blocks.text: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul last week named state Attorney ​General Letitia James as special prosecutor ⁠to look into the case.

U.S. President Donald Trump, a critic of James for years, lambasted the decision to appoint her. "And I feel badly for whoever she's looking at because they won't get a fair shake," he told reporters on Friday.
Asked about Trump's comment, Giuffra said the case shouldn't be politicized. "It has nothing to do with politics," he said.

articles.summary: Following a suspected terrorist plot targeting the UK's Fairford airbase, the US Air Force withdrew all its B-1 planes from the site.

image.caption: US B-1 bombers stationed at RAF Fairford were used for strikes against IranImage: Alastair Grant/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: A week after several men were detained at the Royal Air Force (RAF) base in the UK's Fairford on suspicion of planning terrorist attacks, a Pentagon official announced that the United States had removed its B-1 bombers from the base northwest of London.
On Sunday, aircraft monitoring sites showed the B-1 aircraft flying out of the UK base.

"While operational security precluded us from ​confirming the movement of our assets and forces ​in real-time, ‌we can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have re-deployed to their home ‌stations in the United States," a Pentagon spokesman wrote ‌in ​a statement.

A dozen B-1 bombers had been stationed at RAF Fairford, the British airbase used by the US. London previously allowed the Pentagon to fly sorties out of Fairford against Iranian missile sites which were threatening ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
UK releases air base plot suspects
What do we know about the suspected plot
Last Sunday, police were called to a base in southwest England after a local farmer reported a group of men in several vans engaging in "suspicious" activity.

Investigators blocked off the area and called in the bomb disposal teams. However, no explosives were found in the vehicles. Later, the five British nationals arrested in connection to the incident were released on bail.
US President Donald Trump voiced his disappointment over their release.
On Wednesday, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that Britain had "strong indications" that Iran was involved in a suspected plot targeting the base.
Iran dismissed the accusations as baseless and summoned the British ambassador in Tehran to discuss the issue.

articles.title: Bolsonaro beats expectations in Brazil presidential vote, faces Lula in runoff
articles.summary: A victory for Senator Flavio Bolsonaro would extend a wave of wins across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with US President Donald Trump, while Lula's reelection could be a challenge…

blocks.text: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in the runoff of a presidential election, after the challenger took some 47% of valid votes in the first round on Sunday, October 4, beating the forecasts in most private surveys.

The two leading candidates will advance to the second round of voting on October 25, after topping a field of 12 candidates in a campaign focused on concerns about the growing cost of living, corruption and insecurity in Brazilians’ daily lives.

Bolsonaro, the son of right-wing former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election, now heads to a showdown with the leftist Lula, who picked up 44.9% of votes, with nearly 99% of votes reported.

Private surveys in the run-up to the election had forecast Lula leading the first-round vote by around three percentage points. Bolsonaro’s stronger-than-expected performance will buoy his campaign and may bolster Brazil’s currency and stock market, which have risen on the prospects of the business-friendly challenger.
“The pollsters missed badly,” said Robert Muggah, cofounder of think tank Igarape Institute. “Expect the runoff polls, which show a dead heat, to understate Bolsonaro as well.”

A victory for the senator would extend a wave of wins across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with US President Donald Trump, while Lula’s reelection could be a challenge for Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security.
Despite growing worries over Brazil’s public finances and sluggish economic growth, the campaign offered meager policy debate, as both leading candidates skipped the major TV debates.
SURPRISE SHOWING
Early on Sunday, Bolsonaro told journalists in Rio de Janeiro he was counting on “a protest vote from people who would otherwise vote for another candidate but are opposed to Lula.”
Thaise Lima, a 41-year-old lawyer on her way to vote in Sao Paulo, said her main goal was to get Lula’s Workers’ Party out of office.

“I don’t think Flavio is the best candidate, but I might decide to vote for him in the next few minutes,” she said, adding that she wished psychiatrist and author Augusto Cury were a more viable candidate.
Fernando Tempel, 49, a management consultant, told Reuters he was voting for Bolsonaro despite initially planning to vote for Romeu Zema, the former governor of Minas Gerais state.

“The protest vote foreshadows what is to come in the runoff,” said political analyst Rafael Favetti. “While this should benefit Flavio Bolsonaro now, his growth potential in the second round drops precisely because that support has already been front-loaded.”
ECONOMIC HEADWINDS
Despite falling inequality and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over voters grappling with high living costs, heavy household debt and the threat of crime and more pervasive gang activity.
Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns, while Lula has moved to ban online gambling and, as the race tightened, expanded welfare and proposed fresh debt relief for families.

Rising spending and public debt above 82% of GDP have stoked fiscal concerns that Brazil’s next president will need to address. The government lowered its economic growth forecasts for this year and next to 2.0% and 2.3% respectively.
“I voted for Brazil to start growing again,” said Marciano de Souza e Silva, a 52-year-old public servant in Brasilia who voted for Flavio.

A strong performance by right-wing candidates in Sunday’s Senate election could help Bolsonaro’s ability to pass economic reforms, institute a “more well-behaved fiscal policy” and ultimately boost growth if he is elected, said Marco Saravalle, chief investment officer at MSX Invest/Krivo Capital.
OVERSHADOWED DEBATE
Scandals and fears of foreign interference ahead of the vote largely overshadowed policy debates during the campaign.

Controversy surrounding the now-defunct Banco Master has engulfed much of Brazil’s political class after Daniel Vorcaro, who ran the bank, was arrested earlier this year and accused of a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme.

The investigation has probed the banker’s ties to figures from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to the younger Bolsonaro, who is being investigated for money laundering tied to the case by the federal police. Both have dismissed the allegations against them.
Throughout the campaign, Lula’s allies have warned that the Trump administration might refuse to recognize election results if he wins, pointing to an aborted effort to send US officials to Brazil.
“What is at stake is the future of Brazil,” Lula said after voting in Sao Bernardo do Campo, in Sao Paulo state.
Trump has not formally endorsed a candidate, though he hosted Senator Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly.

Reuters reported on Wednesday that Brazilian intelligence officials briefed a French and German delegation on alleged US and Russian interference before the election. The US has rejected claims ​of interference in Brazil’s affairs.
On Sunday afternoon, Brazil’s electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques said the election was running smoothly.

blocks.text: A man has been shot dead by police in regional New South Wales after allegedly aiming a loaded rifle at officers responding to a car crash.
NSW police were responding to reports that a car had driven into a tree on a road 84km north of Yass about 2.50pm on Sunday.
Officers arrived to find a Chrysler station wagon that had crashed into a tree, with the driver appearing to be unconscious.
Police had been told that the man had a firearm with him in the car, an assistant commissioner, Stephen Hegarty, said on Monday.

“They received information that he took up a firearm in the car and that he was also in the car, not responding to members of the public,” Hegarty said. “That’s why they obviously contacted the police.”
Paramedics were also on the scene.

“Police attended that location and confirmed there was a male still inside that motor vehicle,” Hegarty said. “They approached that vehicle to check on his welfare and medical assistance if required. As they approached that vehicle, they tried to speak and communicate with that person but he did not respond.”
The man then picked up the firearm and pointed it “directly at the police officer”, Hegarty said.
“At that point, I can confirm that police opened fire and he was struck at a number of rounds.”
Police said the gun the man held was loaded.
The police officers were “quite close to the car” when the shooting occurred, Hegarty said.

“They were trying to get to the person to render assistance, to check on his condition.”

articles.title: SC decision clears way for Sara Duterte trial to move forward
articles.summary: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian says the dismissal of the petitions clears the way for Duterte’s trial to proceed

blocks.text: HIGH COURT. The Supreme Court in session.
Supreme Court
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian says the dismissal of the petitions clears the way for Duterte’s trial to proceed

items: The Supreme Court dismissed petitions challenging the Senate impeachment court's decision to lower the voting threshold for Vice President Sara Duterte's conviction, citing lack of legal standing and premature timing.
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian stated that the dismissal allows the impeachment trial to proceed, indicating the court's respect for the Senate's rulings.
The impeachment court's recent ruling allows only senator-judges who are legally and factually capable of participating to vote, requiring 14 votes for conviction among the 20 active senator-judges.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

The Supreme Court’s dismissal of petitions challenging the Senate impeachment court’s voting rules clears a legal hurdle, putting the focus back on Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial, which now moves forward under a basis that allows the number of votes needed for conviction to adjust based on which senator-judges can participate.
The SC, sitting en banc, unanimously junked the three petitions for lacking locus standi, or legal standing, and for being premature, as the trial had not yet reached a final judgment.

The petitions were separately filed by former Marcos administration executive secretary Victor Rodriguez, disbarred lawyer Berteni Causing, and constitutional lawyer Ernesto Francisco Jr. They also sought a temporary restraining order (TRO) and/or writ of preliminary injunction to halt implementation of the ruling while the High Court resolves their petitions.

Rodriguez, now a Duterte ally, had argued that the impeachment court effectively amended the Constitution by adding a qualification not found in its text. Causing and Francisco, for their part, said senators who remain in office should be counted even if they are in hiding, detained, or medically unable to attend the impeachment proceedings.
The High Court, however, junked the petitions on procedural grounds.

“The SC dismissed the separate petitions filed by Victor D. Rodriguez, Berteni Cataluña Causing, and Atty. Ernesto B. Francisco, Jr., challenging the Senate Impeachment Court’s interpretation of the two-thirds vote required to convict in an impeachment case,” the Court said.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said the dismissal of the petitions means the Senate impeachment court could proceed and move forward with the Duterte trial. He said this also indicates the impeachment court is operating “within its bounds and within its constitutional allowance.”

“Two petitions were filed — one was [for] a TRO, and the other was a prayer for status quo ante order. Both were dismissed by the SC, so that means the trial will continue… This also goes to show that the High Court respects the rulings of the impeachment court,” said Gatchalian.

Constitutional lawyer and former Integrated Bar of the Philippines president Domingo Cayosa said the petitions may still be re-filed, but stressed that it cannot undo the decision of the impeachment court, which are final and executory.

He said the swift resolution of the petitions sends a message that the High Court “seemingly leaves it to the Senate impeachment court as the Constitution mandates that they are the sole judge” when it comes to impeachment cases.
“Maybe it would best for the defense to present their evidence, cite the law, and hold on to senator-judges who may vote in favor of their case,” Cayosa told ANC’s Headstart.

Article XI, Section 3(6) of the 1987 Constitution states the Senate has the sole power to try and decide impeachment cases. Conviction requires the concurrence of two-thirds of all the members of the Senate.

On September 23, the impeachment court revisited the basis for determining the number of votes needed for conviction, allowing only senator-judges who were “legally and factually capable” of participating in the proceedings at the time to cast their votes.

This reversed a July 6 ruling by the impeachment court’s presiding officer, Senator Francis “Chiz” Escudero, which treated all 24 senators as the voting baseline. While maintaining the two-thirds threshold, the new ruling allowed the number of votes needed to convict Duterte to be adjusted based on the number of senator-judges legally and factually capable of participating in the proceedings.
With 20 active senator-judges, two-thirds — or 14 votes — will be required for her conviction. Seven votes, meanwhile, are needed for her acquittal. – Rappler.com

Guardian Australia has contacted One Nation for a response.

articles.title: [Ask the Tax Whiz] Will the new audit rules protect honest taxpayers?
articles.summary: Wealth growth alone does not prove evasion. Legitimate sources must be checked, and due process observed.

blocks.text: Part 1 | [Ask the Tax Whiz] Why is the BIR auditing your business?Part 2 | [Ask the Tax Whiz] The BIR sent an audit notice. What now?

In the third and final installment of this series, the Philippine Tax Whiz examines the safeguards under Revenue Memorandum Order (RMO) No. 22-2026—and explains why an annual tax review can help businesses prevent costly disputes without compromising their integrity.
A business can lose money and still pay the correct taxes. A taxpayer can accumulate wealth while concealing taxable income. Effective tax administration must distinguish between the two.

RMO No. 22-2026 strengthens risk-based selection and accountability in a Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) audit. For businesses, however, protection also begins before an audit notice arrives: knowing your tax exposure, keeping reliable records, and choosing credible advisers.
From a global tax policy perspective, predictable enforcement protects revenue, strengthens investor confidence, and allows businesses to grow.
It can reduce arbitrary selection, but fairness depends on reliable data and sound judgment.
RMO No. 22-2026 generally provides system-assisted, risk-based selection for priority cases and anonymized assignment. Mandatory cases follow a different selection process.

These safeguards reduce opportunities for personal influence. They do not replace the obligation to validate discrepancies, consider explanations, and respect due process. Technology should improve the quality of decisions—not merely accelerate them.

Understand the indicators and prepare your explanations. The priority criteria include income tax due below 2% of gross sales or revenues, input VAT exceeding 75% of output VAT, and substantial sales accompanied by a net loss.
These are audit indicators, not automatic tax deficiencies.

A low-margin retailer, an exporter, and a business purchasing equipment have different financial profiles. Risk assessment should account for those differences. Your records should explain why the figures are commercially reasonable and legally supportable.
The order creates no blanket MSME exemption or three-year audit holiday. The general one-eLA rule concerns audit authority for a particular taxable year.
My recommendation remains to reduce routine audit frequency for demonstrably low-risk micro and small businesses, with targeted examinations when credible risk indicators warrant them.
A three-year cycle would require appropriate adoption. Meanwhile, compliance assistance and proportionate enforcement should help small businesses correct problems without unnecessary disruption.
The order already recognizes third-party intelligence, publicly available information, and validated discrepancies as grounds for selecting mandatory cases.

I propose a nationwide, risk-based investigation of potentially undeclared taxable income behind unexplained wealth—including that of high-net-worth individuals and public officials. Authorities should reconcile tax information with lawfully accessible asset, property, and corporate records.
Wealth growth alone does not prove evasion. Legitimate sources must be checked, and due process observed. The same standard should apply regardless of political affiliation, wealth, or influence.
Section V(10) provides for Revalida, or “Audit of Auditors,” through the Tax Audit Review Division, subject to the BIR Commissioner’s approval. The order calls for separate detailed guidelines.
Section VII also identifies unauthorized audit, improper case selection, misclassification, and unjustified reporting delays as grounds for administrative sanctions.

Accountability must extend to public officials and professionals who enable tax crimes. Section 253(C) of the Tax Code prescribes the maximum penalty for a convicted public officer or employee, plus dismissal from public service and perpetual disqualification from holding public office, voting, and participating in elections. For a convicted Certified Public Accountants (CPA), the law expressly provides automatic revocation or cancellation of the CPA certificate. Section 253(B) also makes anyone who willfully aids or abets a tax crime liable in the same manner as the principal offender.
These consequences require criminal conviction—not merely an audit finding. Public office and professional credentials carry responsibilities; neither should shield anyone from accountability.

Routine filing and an Annual Tax Review (ATR) serve different purposes. Filing meets recurring obligations; a review examines whether the returns, records, and tax positions are consistent and adequately supported.
An ATR can reconcile sales across tax returns and financial statements, examine withholding compliance, test VAT claims, and identify documentation gaps before they become disputed findings.
RMO No. 22-2026 does not require an ATR. It is a preventive measure that can complement your accountant’s work—much like a health checkup identifies concerns before they become emergencies.
Potentially, depending on the business’s size and exposure—but no responsible adviser should guarantee savings.

For illustration, ₱10 million in purchases carrying ₱1.2 million in input Value-Added Tax (VAT) represents a material documentation risk. Reviewing invoice validity, eligibility, and reconciliation early can help identify weaknesses and defend valid claims.

Savings may come from preventing errors, avoiding associated penalties, or successfully supporting a position that might otherwise be challenged. A review cannot erase a genuine liability, manufacture missing evidence, or guarantee exemption from audit.
Examine the firm’s credentials, reputation, relevant experience, and methods. Require a clear engagement scope, transparent fees, documented advice, and official payment channels.

Be wary of guaranteed reductions, supposed connections, or requests for unofficial payments. Credible representation means defending supportable positions and pursuing lawful remedies. Where a legal compromise settlement is appropriate, it must meet the applicable requirements and approvals.
To explore an Annual Tax Review or assistance with an existing audit, email consult@acg.ph or visit www.acg.ph for an initial assessment of your needs.
Tax reform should be measured by correct collections, fair treatment, timely resolution, and stronger voluntary compliance—not simply the size of proposed assessments.

For government, that means pursuing serious evasion while respecting taxpayer rights. For businesses, it means investing in compliance before a dispute develops. An annual review can protect your finances; credible advice helps protect your reputation. Neither should require compromising your integrity. – Rappler.com

Mon Abrea, CPA, MBA, MPA (Harvard), is a global tax policy expert and Chief Tax Advisor of Asian Consulting Group (ACGlobal). He advises governments, multinational enterprises, and international organizations on tax policy, investment competitiveness, and fiscal reform. He is the author of Reimagining the World Without Corruption and Why Invest in the Philippines? CREATE MORE Edition, and has represented the Philippines in policy dialogues at the OECD, World Bank, and other international forums.

articles.title: Gillian Anderson responds to backlash after telling ‘distracting’ fans to stop sitting in front row
articles.summary: The actor, who is performing on the West End, was filmed telling theatre fans ‘you can’t come 20 times and sit in the front row, it’ll drive me mad’ Gillian Anderson has come under fire after the…

blocks.text: Gillian Anderson has come under fire after the actor was filmed telling a group of fans that they were “distracting” her by repeatedly sitting in the front row while she performs in London’s West End.

The Sex Education and X-Files star was filmed outside the Soho Place theatre where she’s performing in Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf?, telling a group of fans: “You guys cannot sit in the front row. I do not care; you cannot sit in the front row. It’s so distracting.”
Anderson, who is playing frustrated wife Martha in Edward Albee’s play about an unhappy marriage, then said: “You can’t come 20 times and sit in the front row, it’ll drive me mad.”
The fans, who were not shown in the video, can be heard responding to Anderson’s comments with “I’m sorry” and “I know”.
After the video was uploaded to TikTok, the 58-year-old actor shared a statement on social media in an effort to clarify her position.
“The video doing the rounds is me talking with women I go back over 20 years with – so please don’t say anything negative to or about them,” she wrote on X.
“We’re thrilled to be doing this show but for people in the front row, please be aware that in such an intimate venue we can all see you and sometimes, it can be a tad distracting!”
Anderson signed off with: “That’s all. All good. On with the show and love to everyone and thank you to all of those coming.”

It’s not the first time this year an actor has made headlines with comments about theatre etiquette. Last month, Cate Blanchett asked the audience of her National Theatre production Electra/Persona to put away their phones during curtain call.

“I understand you like filming the curtain call – and it is kind of flattering in a way,” Blanchett said. “But for anyone who is filming the show, please don’t, because it spoils it for the next group of people who come in and are present with us.”

Rosamund Pike criticised an audience member for texting during her West End play Inter Alia in May. “I just wanted to say for anyone going to the theatre, it’s a huge thing that we’re trying to give you,” she told the audience at Wyndham’s theatre.

“Somebody was texting in this part,” she said. “You know who you are … Maybe it was very important, and maybe you’re a doctor, and you’re saving someone’s life, and I hope you are, but we do see these, we do feel them.”

In April, Wicked star Cynthia Erivo halted her one-woman performance of Dracula – in which she played all 23 characters – at the Noël Coward theatre after spotting an audience member illegally recording the show.

In May, The Pitt star Isa Briones told fans to stop yelling references to the medical drama during her Broadway musical Just in Time. And Kristin Scott Thomas, who is due to perform in The Cherry Orchard at the Harold Pinter theatre this month, told the Financial Times she witnessed an audience member eating “a ready meal in the front row once” – but said she still prefers theatre to screen acting, adding: “For me it is telling a story to live, breathing, coughing, eating people and trying to drag them along with you. Which I find incredibly thrilling.”

Other actors, including Andrew Scott, Daniel Craig and Hugh Jackman, have spoken out about the decline in theatre etiquette. Lesley Manville told BBC Radio 4 earlier this year that she finds audience members who take photos during the curtain call “insulting”.
“Clap or don’t clap, but don’t just stick up your phone in our faces,” she said.

It’s not just the performers who have complaints either. Theatregoers at the Royal Shakespeare Company’s The Tempest starring Kenneth Branagh took issue with a baby cooing and gurgling through the first half of a performance in June. The mother and baby were asked to leave the Stratford-upon-Avon theatre for the second half after audience members asked for refunds.

articles.title: [OPINION] Stop asking where UHC will find the money. Build the economy that can pay for it.
articles.summary: How do we make the Philippine economy itself capable of paying for increasingly expensive healthcare?

blocks.text: When Solid North Representative Ching Bernos recently asked where Universal Health Care would get its billions once PAGCOR exits casino operations, she raised a legitimate question. Under the Universal Health Care Act, 50% of the national government’s share of PAGCOR income is earmarked for UHC and transferred to PhilHealth to improve its benefit packages.

With Casino Filipino being privatized as PAGCOR moves toward becoming primarily a regulator, one estimate cited in the current debate puts the resulting annual reduction in UHC funding at around P1.7 billion to P2.1 billion.

P2 billion is not insignificant. But the controversy also illustrates something about how we tend to discuss healthcare financing in the Philippines. The conversation often begins with the same question: Where can government find the money?

We increased tobacco and alcohol taxes and earmarked part of the proceeds for health. PAGCOR contributes gaming revenues. PhilHealth collects premiums. Congress appropriates money to the Department of Health. When additional resources are required, government can borrow from institutions such as the Asian Development Bank and the World Bank.

All of these have legitimate roles. Sin taxes can simultaneously raise revenue and discourage harmful consumption. Gaming revenues already exist and can be redirected toward public purposes. Development-bank financing can fund infrastructure and reforms whose benefits last for decades.

items: Gov’t eyes P353-billion health sector budget for 2027, lower than in 2026
[OPINION] Why Philippine universal health care keeps falling short
[OPINION] Barangay health stations: The heart of universal health care dream
[OPINION] The Philippines is spending more on health, but getting less
Are medical bills free with government’s zero-balance billing?

blocks.text: But these are primarily ways of financing or reallocating resources. There is another question that receives less attention: How do we make the Philippine economy itself capable of paying for increasingly expensive healthcare?

That matters because healthcare is already a massive economic undertaking. According to the Philippine Statistics Authority’s 2025 Philippine National Health Accounts, Philippine total health expenditure reached P1.87 trillion in 2025, equivalent to 6.7% of GDP. Government and compulsory health-financing schemes paid 46.5% of current health expenditure, yet Filipino households still paid 41.2% directly out of pocket.

Universal Health Care therefore cannot ultimately be only a DOH or PhilHealth problem. Those institutions distribute resources, purchase services, and determine benefits. But the money they spend has to originate somewhere in the productive economy.
Our reliance on public-sector financing can also be seen in the country’s relationship with development institutions.

At the end of 2025, the Asian Development Bank reported a Philippine public-sector portfolio of 27 loans worth $10.96 billion. Its outstanding balances and undisbursed commitments for private-sector transactions in the Philippines amounted to $486 million.

The comparison with some neighbors is interesting. In Vietnam, ADB reported a current public-sector portfolio of $2.18 billion and private-sector exposure of $1.42 billion. In Indonesia, ADB reported $7.17 billion in public-sector loans and $1.15 billion in outstanding and undisbursed private-sector transactions.

These are not perfectly equivalent measures, and ADB portfolios should not be treated as a comprehensive measure of how each country’s economy is financed. Countries have different infrastructure requirements, project pipelines and relationships with multilateral lenders. The Philippine ADB portfolio also includes productive investments such as the North-South Commuter Railway as well as programs for nutrition, disaster resilience, employment and investment reform.
Nor does this prove that the Philippines borrows too much or that private finance is inherently better than sovereign lending.
But the contrast raises a useful development question: Are we building enough industries that will eventually generate the income needed to pay for the public investments we are financing today?
The Philippine BPO industry demonstrates what that alternative can look like.
The country’s IT-BPM sector generated approximately $40.3 billion in revenue in 2025 and employed around 1.9 million people, according to IBPAP figures reported by The Philippine Star.
That $40 billion is not government revenue. It would be wrong to compare $40 billion of industry revenue directly with P40 billion in taxes or public expenditure.
But BPO does something more fundamental.

It sells Philippine services to global customers and brings income into the domestic economy. That income pays salaries, suppliers and landlords. Workers pay income taxes and PhilHealth contributions. Businesses pay taxes subject to applicable incentive regimes. Employees buy housing, transportation, education, food and healthcare. The industry also generates foreign exchange.
In other words, BPO first creates economic activity from which households, businesses and government can subsequently draw resources.
Healthcare itself may offer an opportunity to repeat part of that story.

The Philippines already had an estimated $4.2-billion healthcare-services outsourcing industry employing around 190,000 people in 2024. Existing activities include medical coding, chart abstraction, case management and clinical back-office support. The industry’s existing roadmap targets $6.7 billion in revenue and 285,000 full-time employees by 2028, according to CITEM’s Healthcare Philippines industry material.
This could become the foundation of what might be called BPO 2.0.

Instead of competing indefinitely on lower-value transactional work, the Philippines can move toward higher-value healthcare and life-sciences services: clinical data management, pharmacovigilance, biostatistics, medical writing, regulatory support, real-world evidence, decentralized clinical trials, virtual nursing and AI-assisted medical review.

Around that services economy could develop physical industries — medical devices, diagnostics, clinical research, pharmaceutical contract manufacturing and, eventually, more advanced biologics manufacturing.
These are harder to build than call centers. They require predictable regulation, research-capable hospitals, skilled personnel, investment, manufacturing infrastructure and patient confidence.
But they also create capabilities that are harder to automate or relocate overnight.
Consider the scale.
An additional $5 billion in annual healthcare and life-sciences exports would represent roughly P285 billion in gross annual economic activity at P57 to the dollar.

Not all of that would become taxes. Companies have costs and profits. Workers spend their own wages. Some investments receive fiscal incentives. Gross export revenue should never be presented as government revenue.
But the comparison illustrates why the current debate over a P1.7-billion to P2.1-billion PAGCOR funding gap can be viewed from a much larger perspective.
One approach asks:
What existing activity can provide another few billion pesos for UHC?
Another asks:
What new industries can generate another few hundred billion pesos of economic activity from which households and government can finance healthcare?
The Philippines needs both.

Sin taxes should continue to play their public-health and revenue roles. PhilHealth premiums, PAGCOR contributions, and general taxation remain important. Development-bank financing makes sense where the economic and social returns justify borrowing. Better purchasing, primary care, prevention, and governance remain essential because even a richer country can waste healthcare resources.
But economic capacity determines how large the pool of resources becomes in the first place.
Seen this way, UHC is not only health policy. It is also industrial policy.

DTI and BOI matter. FDA efficiency matters. Universities and research hospitals matter. Economic zones matter. So do investors willing to build healthcare-service and medical-manufacturing businesses in the Philippines.

A Filipino nurse providing clinical support remotely to an American health system can generate export income without leaving the country. A Philippine hospital enrolling patients in a multinational clinical trial can attract international research spending. A Filipino physician reviewing safety data for a global pharmaceutical company can sell expertise rather than migrate. A factory producing medical devices can simultaneously create jobs, exports and healthcare capability.
None of this replaces taxation or public financing.
It enlarges the economy beneath them.
That is why the most important question raised by the PAGCOR debate may not be where UHC will find another P2 billion.
It may be this:
What can the Philippines build that generates the next P1 trillion from which UHC, education, infrastructure and social protection can all be paid?
The country built a $40-billion BPO industry by connecting Filipino talent with global demand.
Over the next 25 years, healthcare, life sciences and medical technology could become part of the next chapter.
Finding another source of UHC money matters.
Building an economy capable of continually creating that money matters even more. – Rappler.com

Dr. Jaemin Park is an adjunct professor at the University of the Philippines College of Public Health and works across Southeast Asia on healthcare financing, medical innovation, and public sector reform.

articles.title: Former Bachelor star Sam Wood charged with domestic violence
articles.summary: Fitness influencer, 46, faces court on Monday after his arrest in Noosa at the weekend The fitness influencer and reality TV star Sam Wood has been charged in Queensland with domestic violence…

blocks.text: The fitness influencer and reality TV star Sam Wood has been charged in Queensland with domestic violence offences.
The personal trainer and star of the third season of reality TV show The Bachelor was charged on Sunday and spent the weekend in police custody after an alleged incident on Saturday night.

Mark Watkin, acting CEO of 28 Group, now the parent company of fitness business 28 by Sam Wood, said in a statement on Monday that the company was “shocked and saddened by the matters involving Sam Wood.”
“We have zero tolerance for domestic violence. While the matter is under investigation and before the court, Sam is on indefinite leave from his duties,” Watkin said.
“Our thoughts are with the family and anyone in the community affected by domestic violence.”

A statement posted simultaneously to Wood’s personal Instagram account and that of his wife, Snezana Wood, on Monday morning, said: “This is a difficult time for all of us, we are working through this as a family and are thoroughly co-operating with authorities.”
On Sunday, Queensland police confirmed they had arrested a 46-year-old Victorian man and charged him with domestic violence offences.
The arrest came after officers attended a Noosa address about 9pm on Saturday night after receiving reports of alleged domestic violence.
The man has been charged with assaulting occasioning bodily harm (domestic violence) and strangulation in a domestic setting, police said.
The alleged victim or victims have not been identified.
Wood was refused bail and was expected to appear in Maroochydore magistrates court on Monday.
The personal trainer shot to national prominence when he starred as the eponymous Bachelor in the third season of the reality TV show franchise in 2015.
He met Snezana Markoski when she was a contestant on the show. The couple married in 2018 in Byron Bay. They have four daughters including one from Markoski’s previous relationship.
Wood owns and runs personal training studio The Woodshed in Brighton East, Melbourne.
He built a fitness and nutrition business, 28 by Sam Wood, off the back of his increased profile from The Bachelor, eventually selling the company in 2022 for $71.2m.

Over the past year, the Australian Taxation Office has been pursuing Wood for alleged unpaid tax debts, reported to be in excess of $7 million. Case listings noted in August that a settlement had been reached, with the case dismissed in September.
Wood has recently launched a telehealth-based weight-loss platform aimed at middle-aged women, called Ollo for Women.
Guardian Australia has approached businesses connected to Wood for comment.

articles.title: Yemen’s Saudi-backed government launches military drive to retake all Houthi-held territory
articles.summary:
The announcement came hours after Iranian-backed Houthis reportedly cut a vital supply route to besieged city of Taiz

Yemen’s Saudi-backed government has announced the start of a new…

blocks.text: Yemen’s Saudi-backed government has announced the start of a new military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis, even as the militant group made fresh gains on the ground, reportedly encircling a government-held city.

Rashad al-Alimi, the head of Yemen’s presidential council, said in a statement on Sunday: “I announce today the start of military operations to retake the remaining territories of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory.”

The announcement sets an ambitious goal for the embattled government, which recently lost swathes of the country’s Red Sea coastline and areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait – a chokepoint for international shipping – after a lightning offensive by the Iran-backed Houthis.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government has struggled to roll back the surge, even with the military support of Saudi Arabia. The Houthis have increasingly targeted Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, and on Sunday said they had attacked oil infrastructure in the capital again.
The statement came just hours after the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking the besieged city of Taiz with the government’s interim capital, Aden, according to four security sources.
The Houthi advance followed days of heavy fighting in and around the city.
“We were informed that the Houthis had taken control of the al-Safiya area, where they cut the main road and took control of the police station,” a police source in the area said.

Three sources with the Yemeni military also confirmed Houthi control over the area and the supply route, with traffic along the road halted and the group now surrounding Taiz city. Fighting in the area was ongoing, they added.
Sources from both sides told AFP on Sunday that fighting in and around the western province of Taiz had killed more than 70 people over the past day.

Sources from the internationally recognised government reported that 34 government troops were killed – 20 on the edge of Taiz province in neighbouring Lahj – while Houthi military sources said 39 of their fighters were killed in fighting across Taiz and in border areas with Lahj.

Taiz city itself remains under the control of government forces but has long been besieged from the north, east and west by Houthi fighters and remains one of the main fronts in Yemen’s long-running civil war.

A Houthi military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said on Sunday the group launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi energy company Aramco’s sites in Riyadh and in Khurais area in the east, causing large fires.
The attacks were in response to what the Houthis claimed were 50 Saudi-led ‌air and missile strikes in Yemen in the past 12 hours.
There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia.
Saudi oil exports were already under pressure due to Iran’s blockade of the strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.
The Houthi’s Al-Masirah TV channel reported Saudi strikes on Sunday in the northern governorates of al-Jawf and Saada, saying at least two people had been wounded.
With Reuters and Agence France-Presse

articles.title: NCAP returns in 5 Metro Manila cities
articles.summary: Aside from major roads in Metro Manila, NCAP now expands to these five cities

blocks.text: NCAP. No Contact Apprehension Policy (NCAP) signs dot major intersections along Edsa in Quezon City, ahead of the MMDA's implementation, on May 24, 2025.
Jire Carreon/Rappler
Aside from major roads in Metro Manila, NCAP now expands to these five cities
MANILA, Philippines – The no-contact apprehension policy (NCAP) will be implemented again on Monday, October 5, in the cities of Manila, Muntinlupa, Parañaque, San Juan, and Quezon City.
Valenzuela was also supposed to resume NCAP implementation on Monday, but the city put it on hold due to several ongoing road repairs affecting traffic flow.
The resumption comes nearly three months after the Supreme Court dismissed a petition challenging the policy.

Under NCAP, local governments and the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) can use closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras to detect and record traffic violations. Violators are then issued traffic violation tickets.

blocks.caption: No contact apprehension policy: How it works, how to pay fines, file an appeal

blocks.text: The MMDA began reimplementing NCAP on several major roads in Metro Manila in May 2025 after the Supreme Court partially lifted its temporary restraining order against the policy.
Motorists caught committing traffic violations through NCAP would receive real-time notifications via SMS and email.
The public can check whether they have been recorded committing a traffic violation through the NCAP “May Huli Ka” (You’ve Been Caught) website and eGovPh app.
Rappler also listed some of the top traffic violations in Metro Manila, alongside the corresponding fines.

articles.title: Brazil’s presidential race to go to second round as Flávio Bolsonaro leads incumbent Lula
articles.summary:
Far-right challenger and son of disgraced ex-president Jair Bolsonaro will now face leftwing president in runoff vote

Brazil’s presidential race will go to a second round after the far-right…
articles.byline: Tom Phillips and Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro

blocks.text: Brazil’s presidential race will go to a second round after the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, beat the incumbent leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, but failed to secure the outright majority he needed to avoid a runoff.

With more than 98% of votes counted, the 45-year-old son of the disgraced former president, Jair Bolsonaro, had won 47.3%, meaning he will now face a 25 October showdown with his 80-year-old rival. Lula received 44.8%.

Bolsonaro will go into the second round as favourite and is likely to be boosted by the migration of votes from the election’s other rightwing candidates, who included Ronaldo Caiado, who secured 2.2%, and Renan Santos, who won 2.2%.

Brazil’s far-right put in a stronger than expected showing, with a succession of Bolsonarista politicians winning congressional or gubernatorial races. They included Jair Bolsonaro’s second son, Carlos Bolsonaro, and his wife, Michelle Bolsonaro, who both won seats in the senate. Bolsonaro’s youngest son, Jair Renan, was elected to the lower house of congress. Bolsonaro’s former infrastructure minister, Tarcísio de Freitas, was reelected as governor of São Paulo, Brazil’s most populous and economically important state.

On Sunday morning, as Lula cast his vote in São Bernardo do Campo, the industrial hub in the São Paulo metropolitan area where he began his political career more than half a century ago, the former union leader said Latin America’s largest democracy faced a stark choice.

“People are going to have to choose between strengthening democracy and barbarism,” Lula told reporters, highlighting his adversary’s well-documented links to members of Rio’s underworld, including once employing close relatives of a notorious contract killer.

blocks.caption: Flávio Bolsonaro urged Brazilians to end Lula’s ‘era of backwardness’.  Photograph: Mateus Bonomi/Reuters

blocks.text: After voting in Rio, where the Bolsonaro political dynasty was born in the late 80s, Flávio Bolsonaro urged Brazilians to end what he called Lula’s “era of backwardness”. “I’m more than ready to lead this country and to give Brazilian families the right to dream once again,” claimed Bolsonaro, who has promised an iron-fisted crackdown on crime, despite his ties to members of Rio’s paramilitary mafias.

Lula, who became Brazil’s first elected working-class president in 2002 and was returned to office in 2006 and 2022, is hoping to secure a historic fourth non-consecutive term in this year’s election.

Allies of the veteran leftwinger call the election a crucial battle in the fight against a far-right movement that less than four years ago brought chaos to the capital, Brasília, during an unsuccessful attempt to overturn the result of the 2022 election, when Lula beat the incumbent president, Jair Bolsonaro.
“Brazilian democracy is at stake,” said Talíria Petrone, a leftwing congresswoman from Rio who is seeking reelection.

Speaking at Lula’s final pre-vote rally in Rio, Petrone called for tactical voting to prevent the Bolsonaro clan returning to power. “I’m sure that even those people who don’t like Lula know that Flávio Bolsonaro must be defeated – and the only way is a fourth presidential term for president Lula,” Petrone said.

Bolsonaro hopes winning the presidency will allow him to free his father, who is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a failed coup after refusing to accept he had lost the last election to Lula. Ahead of the election he also called for tactical voting from conservatives who are not supporters of Bolsonarismo, but want to vote Lula out of power.
As well as the president, Brazil’s nearly 159 million voters are choosing state parliamentarians, 27 state governors, 513 members of the lower house and 54 members of the 81-seat senate.

Speaking on the eve of the election, Maria Tereza Fazzio, 74, a retired psychologist from Rio, said she had voted for Lula ever since he first ran for the presidency in 1989 – four years after the end of Brazil’s 21-year dictatorship. She vowed to do so again this year, in order to protect social programmes implemented by Lula and out of fear that a Bolsonaro victory could put her country’s democracy in jeopardy.
“All he talks about is granting an amnesty to his dad and all the others who are in prison [because of the 2022-23 coup attempt] – he hasn’t got any policy agenda,” she said of Bolsonaro.

blocks.caption: A Lula supporter dressed as Our Lady of Aparecida at a campaign rally in Rio de Janeiro on Friday. A row over the saint has caused a nationwide outcry – which could favour Lula, who is Catholic.  Photograph: Pilar Olivares/Reuters

blocks.text: Bolsonaro seemed to have the wind in his sails in the final days before Sunday’s vote, amid public frustration at a cost of living crisis and urban violence.

However, his momentum appeared to have been interrupted by a row involving Brazil’s Catholic patron saint, Our Lady of Aparecida. Speculation that Bolsonaro – who is part of Brazil’s fast-growing evangelical community – might strip the widely cherished patroness of her position caused a nationwide outcry, leaving some to question if it could tip the knife-edge election in favour of Lula, who is Catholic.

On Sunday, an influential Catholic bishops’ organisation, the Episcopal Conference of Brazil, posted a thinly veiled swipe at Bolsonaro on social media. “May God grant us wisdom and courage to build together a reconciled, sovereign, just, and fraternal Brazil,” the group wrote on X, calling on Our Lady of Aparecida to protect the country.

Donald Trump also became a key election issue, with Lula accusing the US president of trying to swing the vote in Bolsonaro’s favour in order to “colonise” Brazil and appropriate its natural resources. Bolsonaro has vowed to build a closer relationship with Trump, who hopes a rightwing victory will help him further cement US control over Latin America after the election of pro-Trump leaders in a succession of countries, including Chile, Colombia and Peru.

articles.title: PSE enters new territory with GCash’s IPO. But to thrive, it must go further.
articles.summary: GCash’s incoming record-setting IPO hints at a stock market opening itself to asset-light enterprises, but is still far from embracing high-growth tech

blocks.text: GCash’s incoming record-setting IPO hints at a stock market opening itself to asset-light enterprises, but is still far from embracing high-growth tech

items: GCash is set to have a record-breaking IPO on the Philippine Stock Exchange, potentially exceeding P55.89 billion, and will debut as one of the top ten most valuable companies in the market.

The company, which operates as a digital application with minimal physical assets, has a strong lead in the e-wallet market with 41.5 million monthly active users, but faces challenges from competitors and a stagnant stock market.
Despite the excitement surrounding GCash's entry, the PSE's strict IPO requirements may hinder the growth of other tech startups, although there is interest from multiple tech firms in going public.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – GCash’s debut on the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) is predicted to be the biggest opening in the market’s history. In terms of IPO, it is set to match or even exceed the P55.89-billion record set by Monde Nissin in 2021 with an expected opening between P53 to P60.9 billion. And, with a post-IPO valuation of P442 billion, GCash will debut in the top ten most valuable companies on the PSE in terms of market cap, alongside the likes of Ayala Corporation and SM Prime Holdings.

The company is entering a stock market largely ruled by traditional businesses in sectors such as banking, utilities, retail, and real estate, among others. On one hand, these are companies that carry vast amounts of physical assets, whether goods, property, or facilities, which drive their valuations. On the other hand, GCash, being a digital application, stands out as an asset-light enterprise.

GCash’s valuation did not come from having a large base of physical assets. As of June 30, Mynt had P237.8 billion in total assets, but just P906.9 million in property and equipment, equivalent to less than 0.4% of the total. Much of the rest consisted of cash, funds held in trust, receivables, and loans. This is in line with the company’s own description of its payments business being able to scale transaction volumes and users without a proportionate increase in physical infrastructure.

Rather, the P442 billion figure would have to be derived from their control in the e-wallet market. According to the company’s IPO summary, GCash has recorded 41.5 million monthly active users during the second quarter of this year, and has four times the active users of its closest competitor. Their lead in Philippine fintech is what is driving their top ten valuation.

blocks.caption: [Vantage Point] GCash at P6.60: Did investors finally get their price?

blocks.text: The excitement for GCash’s debut comes at a turbulent time for the PSE. With only around 280 listed companies, the PSE suffers from being smaller compared to other Southeast Asian markets such as that of Singapore, Vietnam, and Thailand, among others. In recent years, the stock exchange has only shrunk, with more than P580 billion lost due to company exits.

The PSE lacks a high-growth, digital presence. Currently, the stock exchange is dominated by asset-heavy companies. The biggest companies are banks, property developers, utilities, telecom firms, and consumer-serving conglomerates. These are companies that require a lot of investment in property, land, equipment, and other physical assets order to scale, and thus will not see the type of growth that would attract investors the same way that ventures like startups could. Meanwhile, exchanges such as the NASDAQ are led by major tech conglomerates that have been able to scale exponentially, even prior to the boom caused by generative AI.

GCash, which looks nothing like your typical local blue chip, might be just what the PSE needs to shake itself from its stupor. At its P6.60 offer price, Mynt’s roughly P442-billion valuation puts it at about 24.6x its latest trailing 12-month earnings through H1 2026. That is far above the 9.87x price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of the Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) as of October 2. The PSE’s Financials index was even lower at 6.05x P/E. One of the few blue chips trading at a similar premium is port giant ICTSI – the country’s most valuable listed company controlled by the country’s wealthiest man – at 25.53x P/E.

In short, GCash has plenty to live up to if it is to justify that hefty premium. GCash’s entry hopes to shake up the stagnant exchange. However, even in this record-breaking debut, there are still indications of a market set in its ways.

blocks.caption: Yuchengco tells SEC’s Lim: Fresh PSE blood is shareholders’ call

blocks.text: GCash is far from an outsider in the Philippine business world. The fintech company was founded by telecommunications giant Globe, and has continuously received backing from other established conglomerates in the country, such as Ayala Corporation.

While GCash is expected to bring significant growth and activity to the PSE, it is a company entering its maturity phase. Over the course of this year, GCash has recorded slowing growth. The company has already captured the lion’s share of the fintech market, a foothold that will come under pressure from competitors such as Maya. The company hopes that the influx of capital entering through the stock market can help fund their next big push in terms of expanding its ecosystem. (READ: For GCash’s early private equity backers, record IPO will be ultimate payday)

Meanwhile, the PSE’s requirements for IPO listings remain stricter than other exchanges. Currently, a company wishing to enter the PSE must report a net income of either P75 million cumulatively from the past three years or P50 million during the most recent fiscal year. These requirements discourage companies that prioritize growth before profits, such as tech startups.

Elsewhere, exchanges such as the Singapore Exchange and the NASDAQ offer ventures on different paths in order to be eligible. While being too lenient in terms of profit requirements runs the risk of allowing unsustainable companies with no route toward profitability to enter, being as strict as the PSE limits access to only the most successful and matured ventures.

GCash is not the only major tech company eyeing an IPO. Earlier this year, the PSE and Department of Information and Communications Technology reported that as many as 15 tech firms were expressing interest in going public, with the PSE exploring a tech board to open the doors for these firms. Meanwhile, GCash’s largest competitor, Maya, is also planning to go public in 2027.
The question now is if the stock exchange will be able to propel itself with the GCash IPO to lower its gates for more high-growth ventures. – Paolo Vellila/Rappler.com

articles.title: Marcos honors teachers, calls on them to continue forming Filipinos who are discerning
articles.summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Monday, National Teachers' Day, honored teachers and called on them to continue forming Filipinos who are "discerning in thought, principled in action,…

blocks.text: NATIONAL TEACHERS' DAY
Published October 5, 2026 8:00am

President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Monday, National Teachers' Day, honored teachers and called on them to continue forming Filipinos who are "discerning in thought, principled in action, and mindful of the common good."
"Every classroom carries within it the promise of our country's future. It is where young minds learn to question, discover, and dream of what they may one day achieve," Marcos said.

"At the heart of this noble mission are our educators, whose task is to unleash our people's potential and guide them towards greater possibilities in life. Their influence extends far beyond the lessons they impart. By helping children realize what they can become, they also help shape the kind of society we can build," he added.

"On this occasion, we recognize the sacrifices that accompany this profession and reaffirm our shared responsibility to cherish and uplift those who shape our lives. May this celebration also renew our appreciation for their role in advancing Philippine education as well as encourage us to work together in creating an environment where every educator can teach with purpose and every Filipino learner can pursue knowledge with confidence and optimism," the president said.
"I call on our teachers to continue forming Filipinos who are discerning in thought, principled in action, and mindful of the common good," he added.
Marcos then assured teachers that his administration is committed to meet the demands of education.

"This administration is one with you in meeting the changing demands of education and equipping our schools for the challenges of the next generation. Rest assured, this government stands with our educators and nurtures a Bagong Pilipinas where every teacher is given the power to become a source of hope and strength for our children and nation," he said.
"To all our teachers, may the lives you touch remain your greatest legacy to the Filipino people," Marcos added. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Brazil election: Bolsonaro and Lula head to runoff
articles.summary: Populist Flavio Bolsonaro has secured a thin lead over incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, but the next president of Brazil will be decided in the runoff round, according to the country’s electoral…

image.caption: The early count in the Brazilian presidential election puts Flavio Bolsonaro (left) ahead of Luiz Inacio Lula da SilvaImage: Alexandre Meneghini/Pilar Olivares/REUTERS

blocks.text: With votes being counted in Brazil following the presidential election on Sunday, populist Senator Flavio Bolsonaro was leading the race ahead of leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Bolsonaro seeks to continue the right-wing populist movement started by his father, Jair Bolsonaro, while Lula is seeking his fourth non-consecutive term.
With nearly 99% of the ballots processed, Flavio Bolsonaro has received 47.2% of the vote. Lula has 45%, according to the electoral court.
Since neither candidate received enough votes to win outright on Sunday, the court announced that Bolsonaro and Lula will face each other in a runoff.
Bolsonaro is monitoring the vote count in Brasilia, the country's capital, while Lula is following it from Sao Paulo.
Because Brazil uses electronic voting machines, final results are expected to be available within several hours of the polls closing.
You can watch our livestream on the Brazil election results below.
Right gains momentum in Brazil

Fabio de Sa e Silva, a professor of Brazilian studies at the University of Oklahoma, told DW that the right was currently on the rise in Brazil, making it difficult for Lula to change the course of the election.
"He still has a chance, based on the numbers, but the momentum is with the right," said de Sa e Silva.
"The big news tomorrow will be not that we have a runoff... but it is a takeover that happened in Congress by the far-right," the researcher said.
He added that it will be very hard for Lula to govern with Brazil's new Congress, even if he eventually secures another term.
Lula vows to 'defeat the far right'
Lula and Bolsonaro wrapped up their campaigns on Saturday in Brazil's economic powerhouse state of Sao Paulo.

blocks.caption: Long queues of voters were seen in parts of Rio de JaneiroImage: Bruna Prado/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The 80-year-old Lula capped off his campaign with a tour through the city of Sao Paulo, vowing to "defeat the far right."
Organizers said some 150,000 of Lula's supporters turned up for the rally in Brazil's largest city.
Lula has campaigned on continuing his left-leaning Workers' Party platform, comprising welfare programs, state-funded development and income redistribution.
"The people will have to choose between strengthening the democratic regime and barbarism ... between progress and backwardness," he said as he cast his ballot on Sunday.

blocks.caption: The 80-year-old Lula is seeking the presidency for a fourth and final timeImage: Amanda Perobelli/REUTERS

blocks.text: Bolsonaro calls for 'change'

Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, has served as the Liberal Party's senator for Rio de Janeiro since 2019. On Saturday, he led a motorcycle parade through Sao Paulo's countryside cities of Santa Barbara d'Oeste and Americana.
He also held up a portrait of his father, while the crowd shouted "mito" — a Portuguese word for "legend" that Jair Bolsonaro's supporters use to refer to him.

blocks.caption: Flavio Bolsonaro has said he would pardon his father if electedImage: Douglas Shineidr/AFP

blocks.text: The right-wing Bolsonaro has campaigned on hardline security policies and tax cuts, emphasizing high cost of living under Lula, who he has slammed as "incompetent."
"Brazil needs change," the son of the former president said as he cast his vote. "Brazil cannot bear any more suffering, such as high taxes, so many women killed."
Brazil's 2022 election rematch

The elder Bolsonaro is currently serving a 27-year sentence in prison for attempting a coup to overturn his loss to Lula in the 2022 presidential election. Flavio Bolsonaro has vowed to pardon his father if elected.

Lula's team has cast the Bolsonaro movement as a threat to Brazil's sovereignty, pointing to Flavio and Jair's ties with US President Donald Trump, who last year slapped a 50% tariff on Brazilian imports in response to Jair Bolsonaro's coup trial. The US president called the case a "witch hunt."
Brazilians vote in high-stakes presidential election
The younger Bolsonaro has said in interviews he is "more moderate" than his father, who he has nevertheless said will remain "my compass, my point of reference."
Policies where both Bolsonaros are similar include relaxed gun control laws and skepticism of human-caused climate change.
Trump has not endorsed the senator, but has said he is watching the election "very closely."

blocks.caption: US President Trump had held close ties with fellow right-wing populist Jair Bolsonaro [FILE March 2019]Image: Chris Kleponis/CNP/MediaPunch/picture alliance

blocks.text: What happens next?

Brazil finds itself politically divided, and campaigning has been bitter, with online operations from both sides seizing on every gaffe, accusation and rumor, quickly producing slick videos or AI-generated images for social media.

In September, it was revealed Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion tied to the financing of a biopic about his father. He has denied any misconduct.
Who is Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro?

The latest polling for the first round of voting shows Lula at 46% and Bolsonaro at 45%, according to the Brazilian data intelligence and public opinion research firm Quaest cited by Reuters news agency.
In the case of a run-off, the Quaest poll shows Lula at 42% and Bolsonaro at 44%.
In 2022, Lula beat Jair Bolsonaro by only 1.8 percentage points.
Along with voting for president, Brazil's 160 million registered voters are also choosing other lawmakers, governors, and some senators.
